error.message: Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice

root_causes.detail: DeepSeek V4 enables thinking by default even when the request omits the thinking field. Its thinking mode rejects the tool_choice field, while Polaris emitted a forced singleton structured-result choice.

The stream retry classifier treated every aiohttp ClientResponseError as transient, retried the deterministic 400 three times, and propagated an exception without the already-read Provider response body.
The freshness fingerprint used a hand-maintained list that omitted polaris/kernelone/llm and polaris/infrastructure/llm, so the R111 production fixes did not change the alleged source identity.

behavior: On the official DeepSeek Anthropic route, an explicit tool_choice now emits thinking.type=disabled so the forced structured-result protocol remains authoritative.
An explicitly enabled thinking request combined with tool_choice now fails before transport with factory_provider_native_request_thinking_tool_choice_conflict:anthropic_messages.
DeepSeek requests without tool_choice retain the Provider default thinking behavior.
Streaming HTTP retries are now status-aware: 408, 425, 429, and 5xx are retryable; deterministic 4xx failures are not.
Streaming HTTP failures now read at most 501 bytes, preserve at most 500 bytes with a truncation marker, and support both aiohttp read() and iterator-only stream bodies.
Official DeepSeek detection now requires the exact api.deepseek.com host and /anthropic path boundary, while explicit DeepSeek provider identity remains supported.
Backend freshness now fingerprints every production Python source under polaris and factory_bench runtime helpers while excluding test-only modules.
